book.title: The Other Side of Prospect: A Story of Violence, Injustice, and the American City
book.summary: A landmark work of intimate reporting on inequality, race, class, and violence, told through a murder and intersecting lives in an iconic American neighborhood. One New Haven summer evening in 2006, a retired grandfather was shot point-blank by a young stranger. A hasty police investigation culminated in innocent sixteen-year-old Bobby being sentenced to prison for thirty-eight years. New Haven native and acclaimed author Nicholas Dawidoff returned home and spent eight years reporting the deeper story of this injustice, and what it reveals about the enduring legacies of social and economic disparity. In The Other Side of Prospect, he has produced an immersive portrait of a seminal community in an old American city now beset by division and gun violence.

argument.statement: The injustice surrounding Bobby’s wrongful imprisonment reveals how enduring social and economic disparities sustain division and gun violence in American cities.

book.rationale: The book primarily focuses on a murder case and its implications for justice, while also exploring themes of race, inequality, and the social dynamics of an American city.
